landing.evidenceBody: The Work-related Burnout subscale of the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI) was developed by Denmark’s National Research Centre for the Working Environment (NFA). Published validations exist for Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. The World Health Organization describes burnout as an occupational phenomenon, not a medical condition.

diagnosis.a: No. StressCast is a work-wellbeing reflection tool. It does not diagnose, treat or replace a qualified professional.

scenario.a: It is a mathematical what-if: what your score would be if up to two of your items moved one answer category. It is not a forecast, a probability or a confidence interval.

denmark.q: Why does the reference mention Denmark?
denmark.a: The reference values (a mean of 33.0 and 50 as a high-reference mark) come from PUMA, a Danish study of human-service workers. They are context, not a global norm.

email.q: Do I need my email to see my score?
email.a: No. You see your score, the reference and your top driver without any personal data. An email is only needed to receive the full report.

data.a: Before the report step your answers stay in your browser session. When you request the report they are stored to generate and deliver it. During validation, a copy is also sent to the StressCast operator for manual delivery review. Nothing is sent to third-party analytics.

employer.a: StressCast is not designed for employment decisions, and using it to evaluate another person is outside its purpose. There are no employer dashboards of individual results.

accuracy.a: The arithmetic is exact and reproducible. The questionnaire is self-reported, so results depend on context and moment. One measurement is a snapshot, not a destiny.

landing.finalBody: No account, no email, no biometrics. Just seven questions and a transparent result.

report.title: Your StressCast report
report.scenario_note: If up to two drivers move one category. This is not a probability, forecast or confidence interval.
report.currentIntro: This is your current self-reported work-related burnout score on a 0–100 scale.
report.scenarioSubtitle: Mathematical what-if: if up to two eligible drivers change one category.
report.scenarioFooter: Not a prediction, probability, confidence interval or expected change.
report.kImprove: Improve: {k, plural, =0 {no eligible item} one {# item} other {# items}}
report.kWorsen: Worsen: {k, plural, =0 {no eligible item} one {# item} other {# items}}
report.sensitivityBody: One item moving one response category changes your average by 25/7 = {one} points; two items move it {two} points. Limits at 0 and 100 apply.
report.driverNote: These are the items with the highest burden in your answers. They do not prove causality.
report.reverseNote: Reverse-scored item: low energy for family and friends adds burden.
report.pumaBody: PUMA reference (human-service workers in Denmark): mean {mean}, SD {sd}, N = {n}; {share} scored 50 or above; Cronbach alpha {alpha}.
report.deltaAbove: Your score is {points} points above the PUMA mean of {mean}.
report.deltaBelow: Your score is {points} points below the PUMA mean of {mean}.
report.deltaEqual: Your score equals the PUMA mean of {mean}.
report.validityNote: Spanish and Brazilian-Portuguese studies support the reliability of the instrument in those languages, but they do not turn Danish reference values into global norms.
report.planStep1Body: Notice when your top driver (“{driver}”) is strongest. For three days, jot down the time, task and people involved.
report.planStep2Body: Pick one small, reversible change connected to that driver (see the suggestion above). Keep everything else the same.
report.planStep3Body: After several days of stable context, repeat the check and compare with yourself — not with a clinical norm.
report.planNoticeBody: When, where and with whom your top driver is strongest.
report.planTryBody: One small, reversible change related to that driver.
report.planUsefulBody: Your own notes feel different, or a repeat check moves in the direction you hoped. Either one is only a signal.
report.planDontTitle: What not to conclude from one measurement
report.planDontBody: A single score is a snapshot. It does not show a trend, a cause or a condition.
report.formulaBody: Score S = (p1 + … + p7) / 7, where each p is 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100 and p7 = 100 − the direct score. Improve = max(0, S − k·25/7); worsen = min(100, S + k·25/7), with k up to 2.
limitations: Self-reported answers vary with moment and context.
Spanish and Portuguese wording is preliminary until reviewed against validated versions.
PUMA is a Danish human-service sample, not a global norm.
No causal claims: drivers show burden, not causes.
Scenarios are what-if arithmetic, not validated predictions.
report.privacyBody: Used only to deliver this report. During validation a copy goes to the StressCast operator for manual delivery review. Answers and score are never sent to analytics.
report.verificationNote: This ID identifies one issuance of the report, not a person.

emotionally_exhausting.name: Emotional exhaustion at work
emotionally_exhausting.action: Notice which tasks or interactions leave you most drained, and try separating one of them from the rest of your day for a week.

burned_out_due_work.name: Feeling burned out because of work
burned_out_due_work.action: For three days, jot down when you feel most burned out; look for one condition you could change slightly (timing, scope or who is involved).

work_frustrates.name: Work frustration
work_frustrates.action: List this week’s main frustration and choose one small, reversible step: clarify an expectation, batch a task or ask one question.

worn_out_end_day.name: Feeling worn out at the end of the day
worn_out_end_day.action: Try one protected 10-minute pause in the middle of your day and note how you feel at the end of the workday.

exhausted_morning.name: Exhaustion in the morning at the thought of work
exhausted_morning.action: Notice your evening routine and the first 30 minutes of your morning; test one small change and observe what happens.

every_working_hour_tiring.name: Every working hour feeling tiring
every_working_hour_tiring.action: Track the two or three hours that feel most tiring and test changing their order, length or interruptions.

energy_family_friends.name: Low energy for family and friends (reverse-scored)
energy_family_friends.action: Protect one small slot after work with a gentle transition, such as a short walk or music, and note your energy afterwards.

how.title: How StressCast works
how.lead: Everything here can be reproduced with a calculator.
how.calcBody: StressCast calculates a 0–100 work-related burnout score from the seven Work-related items of the Copenhagen Burnout Inventory (CBI). Each response maps to 0, 25, 50, 75 or 100 points and the seven values are averaged. The item about having enough energy for family and friends is reverse-scored.
how.calcNote: The score describes your current self-reported experience. It is not a diagnosis and does not claim that you have a condition. The World Health Organization classifies burnout as an occupational phenomenon, not a medical condition.
how.itemsCaption: Items of the CBI Work-related scale, with their scale type and direction.
how.scenariosBody: The scenarios are not a clinical prediction or a probability. They are a conditional what-if simulation: No change keeps your current score; Improve shows the arithmetic if up to two eligible items moved down one category; Worsen shows it if they moved up one category. One category change in one item moves the average by about 3.6 points (25/7).
how.scenariosNote: The two-item rule is a product sensitivity assumption, not evidence that the change will happen in 30 days.
how.exampleBody: Responses: high, somewhat, somewhat, always, often, sometimes and seldom (energy item, reverse-scored). Burden points: 75, 50, 50, 100, 75, 50 and 75. Mean = 475 / 7 = 67.9. Improve = 67.9 − 2 × 3.57 = 60.7; worsen = 67.9 + 2 × 3.57 = 75.0.
how.exampleCaption: Worked example (illustrative). Items listed in order WB1 to WB7.
how.dataBody: The questionnaire and scoring come from Denmark’s National Research Centre for the Working Environment (NFA). The PUMA material reports, for Work-related Burnout, a mean of 33.0, a standard deviation of 17.7, N = 1,910 and a Cronbach alpha of 0.87; in that population of human-service professions, 19.8% scored 50 or above. Validation studies exist for Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese, but Danish values are not global norms.
how.reliabilityBody: The arithmetic is exact and deterministic. The CBI shows good internal consistency in the cited studies. StressCast v1 has not been validated to predict an individual’s score 30 days later, which is why scenarios are presented as what-if paths and never as probabilities.
how.limitsBody: The score depends on self-report and can vary with moment, context and how you read the questions. The PUMA comparison comes from a Danish sample of human-service professions and is not a global percentile. Do not use the result for employment decisions about another person.

sections.title: Scope and approach
body: StressCast measures work-related burnout with a short self-assessment. Your answers can reveal sensitive information about your wellbeing, so we treat them as highly sensitive operational data even though StressCast is not a medical product.
We follow data minimisation: before you request a report we collect no personal data, and your answers stay in your browser session.

sections.title: What we collect
body: Before the report step: nothing that identifies you. Calculations run without storing your answers.
When you request the report: your email, language, country, answers, result, consent records (with versions and timestamps) and technical delivery status.
Always: minimal technical logs (request identifiers, error codes, a rate-limit key derived from your network address). We do not log answers or payloads.

sections.title: Why we use it and on what basis
body: To generate and deliver your report — based on your explicit consent. Marketing messages require a separate, optional consent that is unchecked by default. Research use would require yet another separate consent and is not performed.
Optional anonymous usage measurement is loaded only if you allow it, and it never includes answers, score, email or report content.

sections.title: Operator copy during validation
body: While StressCast is in its validation phase, a copy of your report request (identifier, answers, result and the PDF) is sent to the StressCast operator so delivery can be reviewed and completed manually. This copy is used only for that purpose, never for employment decisions, marketing or analytics. You are told this before you submit.

sections.title: Who processes data for us
body: Hosting and delivery: Vercel. Database: Supabase. Email: Resend. Bot protection: Cloudflare Turnstile. Rate limiting: Upstash. Model files: Google Drive (never user data). Optional analytics: PostHog (only allow-listed events, after consent). Error monitoring: Sentry (scrubbed of personal data). Payments, only if enabled: Stripe.
Providers act under their own terms and our instructions; transfers outside your country may occur.

sections.title: How long we keep it
body: Individual payloads (answers and results) are kept for 30 days during validation unless a different legal obligation or documented operational need applies. Minimal audit records may be kept longer and contain no answers.

sections.title: Your rights
body: Depending on where you live (for example under the GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, Brazil’s LGPD or Peru’s Law 29733) you may have rights to access, correct, delete, restrict, port or object to processing of your data.
Use the form on the data-rights page. We verify your identity by email before acting.

sections.title: Security
body: Encryption in transit, secrets kept server-side, row-level security in the database, signed and expiring private report links, rate limiting and bot protection.

sections.title: Changes and contact
body: We will update this policy when practices change and publish the date above. Use the data-rights form for any request.

sections.title: Purpose
body: StressCast is a work-wellbeing reflection tool for adults who work. It is not a medical device and does not provide diagnosis, treatment or professional advice.

sections.title: Eligibility and personal use
body: You must be an adult and use StressCast for yourself. Do not complete the check on behalf of another person.

sections.title: Not for employment decisions
body: Results must not be used to make or support decisions about hiring, performance, promotion, discipline or dismissal of any person. Requesting or sharing another person’s result for those purposes is prohibited.

sections.title: Acceptable use
body: No automated scraping, load testing, bypassing of bot protection or attempts to access other users’ reports.

sections.title: No warranty
body: The service is provided as is. Scenarios are what-if arithmetic, not predictions. To the extent permitted by law, the operator is not liable for decisions taken on the basis of the results.

sections.title: Intellectual property
body: The CBI is described in the literature as a public-domain instrument. StressCast’s code, design and copy are protected; do not reproduce them without permission.

sections.title: Changes and law
body: We may update these terms; continued use means acceptance. Governing law and jurisdiction will be set by the operator before public launch.

wellbeing.title: Wellbeing disclaimer
body: StressCast is a work-wellbeing reflection tool. It does not diagnose, treat or replace a qualified professional. It is not an emergency service.
The score reflects your self-reported experience at one moment. A high or low number does not say whether you have a condition.
